paper_diagnosis: Community-acquired Pseudomonas aeruginosa sepsis presenting with ecthyma gangrenosum in a neutropenic infant
disease_label_per_paper: Febrile profound neutropenia with perianal ecthyma gangrenosum and Pseudomonas aeruginosa septic shock
presentation_summary: A 4-month-old ex-preterm girl presented with 24 hours of high-grade fever, lethargy, and poor feeding.
Admission vitals showed hypotension and tachypnea; exam found a violaceous perianal indurated plaque.
Initial labs showed profound neutropenia with ANC 0.08 x10^9/L, leukopenia, CRP 146 mg/L, procalcitonin 11.57 ng/mL, and mild coagulopathy.

Within 24 hours the lesion became necrotic and the patient progressed to septic shock, requiring PICU care, meropenem, CRRT/plasma exchange, mechanical ventilation, and urgent surgical debridement/diverting colostomy.
Blood and wound cultures confirmed Pseudomonas aeruginosa; immune and genetic workup did not identify primary immunodeficiency.
